intent.text: Rate-limit POST /auth/login to five attempts per fifteen minutes per IP and email, counting attempts in Redis and letting logins through if Redis fails.

sequence.title: Add express-rate-limit as a runtime dependency
sequence.summary: package.json gains express-rate-limit ^7.4.0 next to express and ioredis. Nothing else in the manifest moves.

sequence.title: Count attempts in Redis with a fifteen-minute window
sequence.summary: countAttempt increments a per-key counter and sets its expiry only on the first hit, so the window starts at the first attempt rather than sliding.

sequence.title: Wrap the counter in a store that fails open
sequence.summary: failOpenStore adapts countAttempt to the express-rate-limit store interface. If Redis throws, increment reports zero hits, so the request is allowed and a warning is logged.

sequence.title: Build the limiter with five attempts per window
sequence.summary: createLoginLimiter configures rateLimit with the window, a limit of five, draft-7 headers, and a key made of the client IP plus the submitted email.

sequence.title: Put the limiter in front of the login route only
sequence.summary: buildAuthRouter now runs createLoginLimiter() before login. The logout and refresh routes are unchanged and remain unlimited.

sequence.title: Test that the sixth attempt gets a 429
sequence.summary: The new test posts five wrong passwords for one email and asserts the sixth response status is 429.

dependencies.name: express-rate-limit
dependencies.why: Provides the rateLimit middleware that counts requests per key and answers 429 once the limit is passed.

dependencies.name: ../lib/redis.js
dependencies.why: The existing shared Redis client holds the attempt counters so the limit is shared across server processes.

dependencies.name: ../middleware/loginLimiter.js
dependencies.why: The auth router imports the new limiter factory from the middleware module added in this diff.

logic.summary: The expiry is set only when the counter reads 1, so the window is fixed from the first attempt.
logic.failure_mode: If pexpire fails after incr succeeds, the key has no TTL and the counter never resets for that IP and email.

logic.summary: Any error from countAttempt is caught and turned into zero hits, which the limiter reads as under the limit.
logic.failure_mode: While Redis is down, login has no rate limit at all; the only signal is a console warning per request.

logic.summary: decrement and resetKey swallow their own Redis errors with an empty catch.
logic.failure_mode: A failed reset leaves the old count in place until the key expires.

logic.summary: The limiter key combines req.ip with req.body.email, falling back to an empty string when the body has no email.
logic.failure_mode: If the body parser has not run before this middleware, every request from one IP shares the empty-email key.

logic.summary: createLoginLimiter() is called once when the router is built, so all login requests share one limiter instance.

tests.locks: After five login attempts for the same email, the sixth POST /auth/login returns 429.
tests.does_not_cover: The fail-open path when Redis errors, the window expiry, the rate-limit headers, and the logout and refresh routes staying unlimited.

open_questions.text: Is an unlimited login endpoint during a Redis outage the intended trade-off, or should it alert beyond a console warning?
Does the app register a JSON body parser before the auth router, so req.body.email is set when the key is generated?

functions.name: countAttempt
functions.note: Increments login-attempts:<key> in Redis and sets a fifteen-minute expiry on the first hit. Returns the new count.

functions.name: failOpenStore
functions.note: Returns an express-rate-limit store whose increment fails open on Redis errors and whose decrement and resetKey ignore errors.

functions.name: createLoginLimiter
functions.note: Builds the rateLimit middleware with a limit of five per window, keyed by IP and email, backed by failOpenStore.

functions.name: buildAuthRouter
functions.note: Now inserts the login limiter before the login handler; the other routes are untouched.

functions.name: attempt
functions.note: Test helper that posts one wrong-password login for ada@example.com.
